issues.evidence: Tibetan "བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་ཉིད་རྟག་ཏུ་གཏང་མི་བྱ" has the negative "གཏང་མི་བྱ" (one should not forsake, ever); Sanskrit "न विमोच्यं हि सदैव बोधिचित्तम्" likewise negative; bo-shenga 1-8 "གཏང་བར་མི་བྱའོ". The English reverses the injunction.
Tibetan "ངང་པ" is a goose or swan (haṃsa), not a peacock; bo-shenga 2-5 "བྱ་ངང་པ" (the bird, swan/goose) and bo-gyaltsab 2-5 "ངང་པ་ཤིན་ཏུ་སྐད་སྙན་ཡིད་འོང་ལྡན".
issues.fix: Possessing swans with highly sweet and pleasing voices,

issues.evidence: Tibetan "དེ་ཡང་བདག་གིས་མ་བསྟེན་ཏོ" is negative (I did not rely on that); Sanskrit "मया तच्च न सेवितम्"; bo-shenga 2-41 "བསོད་ནམས་དེ་ཡང་བདག་གིས་རང་གི་རྒྱུད་ལ་མ་བསྟེན་ཏོ"; bo-gyaltsab 2-41 "ཞེས་པ་དགེ་བ་མ་བྱས་པས་འགྱོད་པའོ" (regret at not having done virtue). The English asserts the opposite.
issues.fix: I have not relied upon that.

issues.span: Leave these wandering beings in blindness
issues.evidence: Tibetan "འགྲོ་འདི་ལྡོངས་པར་མི་དགོད་ཅིང་" contains the negation "མི་དགོད" (do not leave/place in blindness); Sanskrit "मा भूदन्धमिदं जगत्" (let this world not be blind). The English turns the plea into its opposite.
issues.fix: Do not leave these wandering beings in blindness,

issues.evidence: Tibetan "བསྐལ་པ་བྱེ་བ་བརྒྱར" is a hundred "bye ba" (ten millions), i.e. a billion; Sanskrit "कल्पकोटिशतैरपि" (hundreds of koṭis); bo-kunpal 4-19 "བསྐལ་པ་བྱེ་བ་ཕྲག་བརྒྱར". "Hundred thousand" is the wrong number.
issues.fix: a hundred times ten million eons (a billion eons)

issues.span: The enemies, hatred, and so forth,
issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཞེ་སྡང་སྲེད་སོགས" lists hatred and craving (locked terms ཞེ་སྡང "hatred", སྲེད "craving"), then "and so forth"; Sanskrit "तृष्णाद्वेषादि"; bo-shenga 4-28 "ཞེ་སྡང་དང་སྲེད་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ". Craving is missing from the English.
issues.fix: The enemies, hatred, craving, and so forth,

issues.span: One should forsake the greater for the sake of the lesser;
issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཆུང་ངུའི་ཕྱིར་ནི་ཆེ་མི་གཏང་" is negative: do not abandon the greater for the lesser; Sanskrit "नेतरार्थं त्यजेच्छ्रेष्ठाम्" (na ... tyajet). The English reverses the instruction.
issues.fix: One should not forsake the greater for the sake of the lesser;

issues.evidence: Locked term ཤེས་བཞིན "introspection"; Tibetan "ཤེས་བཞིན་མྱུར་དུ་ལྡང་སེམས་ལ" (Sanskrit संप्रजानन्). The translation uses "vigilance".
issues.fix: With introspection, to the thought of rising quickly,

issues.evidence: Tibetan "བསྐལ་པ་སྟོང་དུ་བསགས་པ་ཡི" means accumulated over a thousand eons; Sanskrit "कल्पसहस्रैः" (thousands of eons). "Ten" is wrong.

issues.span: Do not regard even their own bodies for their sake;
issues.evidence: The relative "གང་ཕྱིར" and "དེ་ལ" refer to sentient beings, for whose sake the lords (buddhas) disregard their own bodies (bo-kunpal 6-121 "སེམས་ཅན་གང་གི་ཕྱིར་དུ་རང་གི་སྐུ་ལའང་མི་གཟིགས་པར་མཛད་པ"; bo-gyaltsab 6-121 "སེམས་ཅན་གང་གི་ཕྱིར་དུ"). In the English, "their sake" and "them" can be read as the lords themselves.
issues.fix: Do not regard even their own bodies for the sake of those beings;

issues.evidence: Tibetan "ནུས་ཀྱང་ཕྱིར་གནོད་མི་བྱེད་དེ" is negative (although able, they do not harm back); Sanskrit "विकर्तुं नैव शक्नोति" (cannot/does not harm). The English says the farsighted do retaliate.
issues.fix: do not harm him in return.

issues.span: the boat of a divine body
issues.evidence: Tibetan "མི་ཡི་གྲུ" is the boat of a human (body); Sanskrit "मानुष्यं नावम्". "Divine" is wrong.
issues.fix: the boat of a human body

issues.evidence: Tibetan "བྱང་ཆུབ་ཐོབ་པར་མི་འགྱུར་རོ" is negative (I will not attain awakening); Sanskrit "न च बोधिर्भविष्यति". The English reverses the claim.
issues.fix: I will still not attain awakening.

issues.evidence: Locked term ལྷག་མཐོང "special insight"; Tibetan "ཞི་གནས་རབ་ཏུ་ལྡན་པའི་ལྷག་མཐོང་གིས". The translation uses "superior insight".
issues.fix: By special insight fully endowed with calm abiding

issues.span: Since others take a share of the suffering,
issues.evidence: Tibetan "སྡུག་བསྔལ་སྐལ་གཞན་མི་ལེན་ན" is negative (others do not take a share); Sanskrit "नान्यस्य तद्व्यथाभागः". The point of the verse (loved ones cannot share one's suffering) is reversed.
issues.fix: Since others do not take a share of the suffering,

issues.evidence: Tibetan "ཞི་བའི་ནགས་ཀྱི་ནང་དག་ཏུ" mentions only peaceful forests; Sanskrit "शान्तासु वनभूमिषु" (peaceful forest lands). "Mountain caves" is not in the source.

issues.span: Ultimate truth is the domain of the intellect;
issues.evidence: Tibetan "དོན་དམ་བློ་ཡི་སྤྱོད་ཡུལ་མིན" is negative (not the domain of the intellect); Sanskrit "बुद्धेरगोचरस्तत्त्वम्". The English reverses the core point.
issues.fix: Ultimate truth is not the domain of the intellect;

issues.span: Stated that the mind sees the mind.
issues.evidence: Tibetan "སེམས་ཀྱིས་སེམས་མི་མཐོང་ཞེས་གསུངས" is negative; Sanskrit "चित्तं चित्तं न पश्यति". The English asserts the opposite.
issues.fix: Stated that the mind does not see the mind.

issues.evidence: Tibetan "འཇམ་དབྱངས" is Mañjuśrī (locked term "Mañjuśrī"); Sanskrit "मञ्जुघोषपरिग्रहात्". Wrong figure.
